system:
You are working out the chronology of a compulsory third party motor accident claim in New South Wales, from a list of things recorded about decided claims.

Divide the life of a claim into ordered PHASES, and place every recorded item in the phase at which the thing it measures COMES INTO EXISTENCE -- not when it is written down, and not when it is used.

Work out from each definition what the measured thing IS, and place it when that thing comes into being. Some definitions carry their own timing: a condition described as pre-existing is one the claimant had beforehand. Others do not, and for those you must reason about the claim.

That distinction decides most of the hard cases:
  * A medical assessment performed years later measures a physical state that arose at the time of the injury. Ask when the QUANTITY was fixed, not when it was measured.
  * Something recorded in the final decision may describe a fact established long before it.
  * A procedural fact about how the claim was run belongs to the phase in which the claim was run, not to the injury.

Decide how many phases there are. Use as few as genuinely capture the order and no more; a phase containing one item is fine if that item really stands alone in time. Items that arise at the same stage belong in the same phase, and a phase may contain items that cause one another -- being contemporaneous is not being simultaneous.

For every item, say in one sentence WHEN the thing it measures came into existence. That sentence is the justification for its placement and will be recorded.
user:
Recorded about each decided claim:
  - Lump Sum: the total dollars awarded to the claimant
  - WPI %: whole person impairment as a percentage: a clinical assessment of the permanent impairment remaining once the claimant's condition has stabilised
  - Non-Economic Loss: dollars awarded for pain and suffering, as a component of the payout
  - Future Economic Loss: dollars awarded for loss of future earning capacity, as a component of the payout
  - Claimant Weekly Income: the claimant's weekly earnings before the accident
  - Claimant Age: the claimant's age in years at the date of injury
  - Claimant Gender: the claimant's recorded gender
  - Nature: which procedural route the claim took: approval of an agreed settlement, or a contested damages assessment
  - Injury Burden Intensity: the overall physical severity of the injuries the claimant sustained in the accident
  - Treatment Burden: the extent of treatment, surgery and ongoing care the claimant underwent for those injuries
  - Work Impact Severity: how much of the claimant's capacity to work was lost
  - Legal Procedural Complexity: how straightforward or contested the components of the payout were to determine
  - Psychological Injury Emphasis: how much the psychological damage was discussed in the court case. It is an observed indicator of an underlying psychological injury which is not itself recorded anywhere in the data
  - Liability Clarity: how obvious it is who was at fault in the accident
  - Causation Complexity: how straightforward it is to determine how much of the claimant's current physical health, psychological health, and ability to earn an income is due to the accident rather than to other causes
  - Pre-existing Condition Salience: the physical and psychological health conditions the claimant had before the accident

Define the ordered phases of a claim, then place every item in one.

phases.name: Pre-Accident
phases.description: This phase includes all factors existing before the accident that have a bearing on the claim.

phases.name: Accident and Immediate Aftermath
phases.description: This phase includes the accident itself and the immediate physical and psychological results, including the initial treatment requirements.

phases.name: Claim Processing and Investigation
phases.description: This phase includes the process of determining clinical assessments, processing the claim, and understanding the components that will inform the final compensation decision.

phases.name: Resolution and Payout Decision
phases.description: This phase involves settling the claim either through negotiation or adjudication and determining the lump sum awarded to the claimant.

assignments.when_it_arises: The Lump Sum is determined when the claim is resolved and a final compensation amount is decided.
The WPI % comes into existence when medical assessments determine the percentage of whole person impairment.
Non-Economic Loss is awarded as part of the final resolution of the claim.
Future Economic Loss is determined as part of the resolution of the claim.
The Claimant Weekly Income existed as a factual financial state before the accident.
The Claimant Age is a factual detail about the claimant at the date of injury.
The Claimant Gender exists as a characteristic of the claimant existing before the accident.
The procedural nature of the claim is determined during the claim processing phase as the claim's course becomes established.
The Injury Burden Intensity arises from the physical injuries sustained in the accident.
The Treatment Burden is understood over time as treatment is received after the accident.
Work Impact Severity is determined during the assessment of the claimant's capacity to work as affected by the accident.
Legal procedural complexity is understood during the processing of the claim as the elements to be resolved become complex or straightforward.
Psychological Injury Emphasis is developed during the handling of the case and its discussions.
Liability Clarity emerges from the initial assessment of the accident circumstances.
Causation Complexity becomes apparent during the investigation into whether health and income issues are linked to the accident.
Pre-existing Condition Salience arises from the claimant's health state before the accident.
